although I don't think the cramps were physical, I think they were more mental,
I was very tightened up, I was very emotional,

but I actually think that the cramps helped me in a way.
I think that I let go, I kind of hit my shots a bit more,
and just let go.
And, yeah, then of course the fifth set went my way
and I'm happy about that
and happy to be sitting next to this beautiful trophy

Good evening, congratulations.

I was struggling a lot with a lot of physical issues,
I was struggling with my tennis, I just didn't play well.
And, I mean, for sure this trophy helps the belief a lot.
So, I think, yeah, as you said, I'm far away from that moment right now.
I think last year was one of the most difficult moments in my tennis career,
and this year it's one of the happiest moments in my tennis career,
and it's a very different feeling right now.

do you think it can really change the way you approach the slams

Hey Sasha, congrats on your win. I wanted to know what you went through your mind when
after the match point when you fell down on the court. I think it was a moment you
thought a lot before. What went through your mind at this exact moment? Was it relief or

first of all I didn't believe that I won and then I saw my box and they all

of my tennis career.

I lost the Grand Slam final here, so all of those memories for me,
they're not wiped out, they'll still be with me,

coaches even longer, so I think everybody deserves this trophy equally.
